evals.prompt: I run TrailKit (trailkit.co.uk), a UK online shop for hiking and trekking gear with a content blog. I've attached our full content inventory (CMS export with GA4 sessions) and the content inventories our virtual assistant compiled for our two main competitors, Summitline Outdoors and PeakPath. We have no SEO tools connected — these three files are everything we have. What content are we missing compared to them, what should we create first, and why?
evals.expected_output: A gap report built strictly from the three fixtures: winter hiking, hiking with dogs, and wild camping/access identified as missing-topic gaps with competitor coverage and own-site absence both cited; boot waterproofing recognized as already covered by /blog/boot-care-guide instead of reported as a gap; navigation classed as a depth gap; glossary/tool/video format gaps surfaced with GEO framed as opportunity rather than measured citations; priorities computed with the skill's scoring model and visible arithmetic; volumes estimated-labeled and fixture numbers attributed as user-provided.
expectations: Traceable planted topic gaps: the analysis identifies winter hiking (Summitline's 9-article 'Winter skills & gear' cluster plus PeakPath's 4-article 'Winter hiking' cluster vs zero winter pages in the TrailKit inventory), hiking with dogs (Summitline 5 + PeakPath 3 articles vs zero), and wild camping/UK access (PeakPath's 4-article 'Wild camping & access' cluster vs zero) as missing-topic gaps — each stated with BOTH sides: the competitor coverage as it actually appears in the competitor fixtures and the absence from the own-site inventory, per the Output Validation item 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)'.

False-positive guard: boot waterproofing is NOT reported as missing content — TrailKit's /blog/boot-care-guide ('Complete Boot Care: Cleaning, Conditioning and Re-Waterproofing') already covers it, and the analysis either leaves waterproofing off the gap list or explicitly notes it as covered (citing that URL), at most classing it as a depth/angle/format observation against Summitline's waterproofing articles — a recommendation to create net-new waterproofing content as a gap fill fails.

Like-to-like coverage comparison: a topic-level comparison (matrix or equivalent) reports counts consistent with the fixtures, includes at least one correctly-marked covered/no-gap row (e.g., foot care/blisters — TrailKit's blister-prevention article vs PeakPath's trail-blister article — or clothing/layering, which TrailKit and Summitline both cover), and classes navigation as a DEPTH gap (TrailKit's single map-and-compass article vs Summitline's 6-article navigation cluster with GPS watches and apps) rather than a wholly missing topic — per the reference's gap categories (topic vs depth) and the Output Validation item 'Gap analysis compares like-to-like content (topic clusters to topic clusters)'.

Format gaps from fixtures with honest GEO framing: at least two of the three planted format gaps are surfaced — glossary/definition content (Summitline's 60-term glossary vs none at TrailKit), interactive tools (Summitline's rucksack size calculator), video (PeakPath's 18-video route series) — and any GEO/AI-visibility angle is framed as an opportunity type (definition/Q&A content suits AI answers) WITHOUT asserting measured AI-citation data for any site, since no ~~AI monitor is connected and the fixtures contain none.

Prioritization follows the skill's own scoring scheme with the arithmetic shown: gaps are prioritized using the reference's model — the 5-factor Gap Priority Score (Search Demand 25% / Competitive Density 20% / Business Relevance 25% / Creation Effort 15% / Conversion Potential 15%) and/or the Quick Win Score = (Search Demand + Business Relevance) − (Creation Effort + Competitive Density) — with per-gap factor scores visible, at least one computation written out so a grader can re-run it, the arithmetic correct, and tier placement (P0–P3 per the reference's ranges, or Tier 1 Quick Wins / Tier 2 Strategic Builds / Tier 3 Long-term per SKILL.md Step 9) consistent with the computed scores; an ordering asserted with no scoring model applied fails.

No fabrication and clean source labels: no competitor topic, article count, URL, or traffic figure appears that is not in the fixtures (topic ideas beyond them are permitted only when framed as untapped/'no competitor covers this' suggestions, never attributed to competitor coverage); every search-volume or difficulty figure is explicitly labeled estimated or an explained N/A — never presented as tool data, since no SEO tool is connected — with such labels living in the analysis tables and source notes while proposed page titles and calendar-entry titles stay free of workflow markers; fixture numbers (GA4 sessions, VA-crawl counts, traffic estimates) are attributed as user-provided, per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~analytics data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or estimated)'.

evals.prompt: TrailKit again (trailkit.co.uk). Before our 7-day SEO tool trial expired we exported its content-gap keyword report — keywords Summitline or PeakPath rank for that we don't — with volume, difficulty, their position and their URL (attached). Our own inventory and both competitor inventories are attached too. Turn this into a keyword-gap plan: which keywords do we go after, in what order, and is there anything in the export we should NOT chase?
evals.expected_output: A keyword-gap plan sourced from the export: CSV figures labeled tool-sourced and additions estimated; 'how to waterproof hiking boots' caught as already covered by /blog/boot-care-guide and reframed as a strengthen-existing-page play; 'campervan insurance uk' filtered on business relevance despite being the export's highest-volume row; the remaining keywords bucketed into High Priority / Quick Wins / Long-term consistently with their volume and KD; the order justified by the skill's scoring arithmetic; no positions or URLs invented beyond the export.
expectations: Source discipline across the two data classes: figures taken from the attached CSV are labeled as tool-sourced (the user-provided SEO-tool export) wherever they are used, and any keyword or metric the analysis adds beyond the export is explicitly labeled estimated — the two sources are never blended without labels, per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~analytics data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or estimated)'.

Export trap caught: 'how to waterproof hiking boots' (1,600/mo, KD 24 in the export) is flagged as ALREADY COVERED by TrailKit's /blog/boot-care-guide ('Complete Boot Care: Cleaning, Conditioning and Re-Waterproofing') — recommended, if at all, as strengthening/expanding that existing page (a depth or ranking play), never as a missing-content keyword requiring net-new content; presenting it as an uncovered gap fails.

Keyword-gap categorization per SKILL.md Step 4 — High Priority (high volume, achievable difficulty), Quick Wins (lower volume, low difficulty), Long-term (high volume, high difficulty) — with assignments consistent with the export's numbers: 'best gps watch for hiking' (5,400/mo, KD 52 — the export's highest difficulty) is NOT presented as a quick win, and at least two of the four KD ≤ 16 rows ('what is scrambling' KD 12, 'rucksack size calculator' KD 9, 'dog hiking boots' KD 15, 'hiking first aid kit list' KD 16) appear among the quick wins.

Business-relevance filter applied per the reference's gap filters ('Business relevance — must relate to your product/service'): 'campervan insurance uk' (8,100/mo — the export's highest volume) is excluded or explicitly deprioritized with the reasoning stated (TrailKit sells hiking gear, not insurance) and does not appear among the top content recommendations on raw volume.

Prioritization arithmetic shown on export numbers: the recommended order is justified by the skill's documented scoring (the reference's 5-factor weighted Gap Priority Score and/or the Quick Win Score formula), with factor scores visible for scored gaps and at least one computation written out and arithmetically correct — a ranking that just mirrors descending volume with no scoring model applied fails.

No fabrication: every keyword-gap claim traces to a CSV row (keyword, volume, KD, competitor, position, URL as exported) or is explicitly marked an estimated addition; no competitor position, ranking URL, or keyword is invented beyond the export; claims about TrailKit's existing coverage trace to the own-site inventory fixture.

evals.prompt: Καλησπέρα! Έχουμε κέντρο φυσικοθεραπείας στη Θεσσαλονίκη (efkinisia-physio.gr). Σας επισυνάπτω την πλήρη λίστα του περιεχομένου μας (εξαγωγή από το CMS, με επισκεψιμότητα από το GA4) και την καταγραφή που έκανε η συνεργάτιδά μας για τα δύο ανταγωνιστικά κέντρα που παρακολουθούμε. Δεν έχουμε συνδεδεμένα εργαλεία SEO — μόνο αυτά τα δύο αρχεία. Τι περιεχόμενο μάς λείπει σε σχέση με τον ανταγωνισμό; Τι να γράψουμε πρώτο και γιατί; Θέλουμε και προτεινόμενους ελληνικούς τίτλους για τα άρθρα που θα φτιάξουμε.
evals.expected_output: A native-Greek gap report built only from the two Greek fixtures: πρόληψη πτώσεων/τρίτη ηλικία, αθλητικές κακώσεις δρομέων and πελματογράφημα/ορθωτικά identified as missing topics with both sides cited; «ασκήσεις για τον αυχένα» recognized as covered by the clinic's own αυχενικό-σύνδρομο service page; FAQ and video surfaced as format gaps; priorities scored with the skill's model and shown arithmetic; every volume marked εκτίμηση; proposed article titles in clean native Greek with no workflow labels inside them.
expectations: Native-Greek deliverable: the report is fluent, idiomatic Greek throughout (correct diacritics and final-sigma use, no translation-ese or untranslated boilerplate headings), phrased in a register a Greek clinic owner would accept — including the proposed article titles, which read as natural Greek health-content titles. Of this, only the diacritics, final-sigma, and untranslated-boilerplate checks are graded structurally at Mode B; fluency, register, and title-naturalness judgments are not eyeballed — this eval's fresh Greek prose output is flagged for the binding greek-content-editor pass at Mode B time.

Traceable planted gaps, both sides cited: at minimum, πρόληψη πτώσεων/φυσικοθεραπεία τρίτης ηλικίας (Ανάπλαση 4 άρθρα + Κίνηση 2 άρθρα vs no related page in the own-site inventory), αθλητικές κακώσεις δρομέων (Κίνηση 5 άρθρα vs none), and πελματογράφημα/ορθωτικά πέλματα (Ανάπλαση 3 άρθρα + σελίδα υπηρεσίας vs none) are identified as missing topics — each citing the competitor coverage as it appears in the fixture AND the own-site absence.

Greek false-positive guard: «ασκήσεις για τον αυχένα» is NOT claimed missing — the analysis matches Ανάπλαση's neck articles («Ασκήσεις για τον αυχένα στο γραφείο», «Αυχενικός πόνος από το κινητό») against the clinic's own /ypiresies/afheniko-syndromo («Αυχενικό σύνδρομο: θεραπεία και πρόγραμμα ασκήσεων για το σπίτι») and cites it as existing coverage; at most a depth/angle/format observation (e.g., the text-neck angle) is acceptable — a 'create neck-exercise content' gap recommendation fails.

Format gaps with honest GEO framing: the FAQ gap (Κίνηση's 12-question FAQ hub vs none on the own site) and the video gap (Ανάπλαση's 25 embedded exercise videos vs none) are surfaced; the FAQ/Q&A gap may carry a GEO/AI-answers rationale as an opportunity type, but no measured AI-citation data is asserted for any site (no ~~AI monitor is connected).

Placement-aware labeling: estimation and workflow markers (εκτίμηση/est., explained N/A cells, data-needed notes) live in the analysis tables and source notes — the proposed Greek article titles and any content-calendar titles, i.e. copy meant to be reused as-is, contain no such workflow or agency labels; a proposed title embedding a bracketed marker fails.

Prioritization per the skill's scheme with metrics honestly labeled: priorities come from the reference's scoring model (the 5-factor weighted Gap Priority Score and/or the Quick Win Score) with at least one computation written out and arithmetically correct; every search-volume/difficulty figure is labeled εκτίμηση (or an explained N/A) since no SEO tool is connected, and the fixtures' GA4 and crawl numbers are attributed as user-provided.

No fabrication: no Greek competitor topic, article, count, URL, or traffic figure appears beyond the two fixtures; ideas beyond them are framed only as untapped-market suggestions not attributed to competitor coverage; no clinical-demand statistics or patient-behavior figures are invented.

evals.prompt: TrailKit once more (trailkit.co.uk) — same three inventory files, still no SEO tools connected. Run the content gap analysis, and then for each top gap tell us what happens next in your skills library: which skill takes it onward and exactly what context you would hand over, so we can run that skill without re-explaining everything. We want demand validated before anyone writes a word.
evals.expected_output: The gap analysis plus explicit onward routing per the library's handoff convention: gap keywords go to keyword-research for demand validation and chosen builds to seo-content-writer, each with a handoff block carrying the CLAUDE.md payload fields — the CORE-EEAT/CITE score slots honestly marked not yet available since no audit has run; the downstream skills' work is not performed inline; every routed gap is one of the fixtures' planted gaps and the waterproofing false positive is not handed off as net-new.
expectations: Routing to keyword-research for demand validation: the response explicitly names keyword-research as the next skill for validating/deep-diving the gap keywords (consistent with Related Skills: 'keyword-research — Deep-dive on gap keywords') and provides a handoff context block for it carrying at least the target keyword(s)/topic, intended content type, and site/content URL context, per the CLAUDE.md inter-skill handoff convention.

Routing to seo-content-writer for the build: gap items chosen for creation are routed to seo-content-writer (consistent with Related Skills: 'seo-content-writer — Create gap-filling content') with their own handoff context (target keyword, content type, where the content will live); routing the covered boot-waterproofing topic to a refresh path for the existing /blog/boot-care-guide page (e.g., via content-refresher) is acceptable and correct.

Handoff payload honesty: the CLAUDE.md payload fields that do not exist yet — CORE-EEAT dimension scores, CITE scores, priority item IDs from an audit — are marked not yet available/pending (no audit has run in this conversation) rather than filled in; a handoff block asserting concrete dimension scores (e.g., 'C:75 O:60 R:80 E:45') or CITE numbers fails as fabrication.

Boundary kept — the downstream skills' jobs are not performed inline: no completed keyword-research deliverable (no opportunity-scored keyword report or 4-form Greek dual-coverage expansion presented as finished research) and no drafted article or page copy appears; keyword mentions stay framed as gap findings for keyword-research to validate, and the delivered scope of this response remains the gap analysis plus routing.

Routed gaps are traceable to the fixtures: every gap handed onward is one of the planted gaps (winter hiking, hiking with dogs, wild camping/access, navigation depth, or the glossary/tool/video format gaps) with its fixture evidence intact; the boot-waterproofing false positive is not handed off as a net-new content gap.

No fabrication: no competitor data beyond the three fixtures; any volume/difficulty figure in the analysis or handoff context is explicitly labeled estimated (no SEO tool is connected); no prior audit results, hot-cache memory, or tracked-gap history is claimed from memory-management, since none exists in this conversation.

evals.prompt: Find the content gaps between my site verdantia-roofs.co.uk and my three competitors sedumline.co.uk, greenlid-roofs.co.uk and urbancanopy-living.co.uk. We install sedum and wildflower green roofs across the UK. I haven't given you anything else — no exports, no inventories, no analytics — and we have no SEO tools connected. Just tell me what they cover that we don't.
evals.expected_output: No gap list is produced or invented: the response explains that gap analysis needs both real inventories, requests the skill's manual-data inputs (own content inventory, competitor content data, optional performance data and goals), attributes nothing specific to the three named competitor domains, and offers only clearly process-framed scaffolding for when the data arrives.
expectations: The response asks for the skill's manual-mode inputs instead of delivering a gap list: per Data Sources ('With manual data only: Ask the user to provide...'), it requests at minimum the user's own content inventory (or a representative sample); and because the three competitor URLs are already supplied while their content is not, it also requests competitor content data for those sites — the Step 3 (Analyze Competitor Content) input that the with-tools path would pull from ~~SEO tool and that only the user can supply here; also asking for traffic/keyword performance, known strengths/weaknesses, or business goals matches the documented list.

No observed-coverage claims for the named domains: nothing specific — topics, article counts, URLs, content formats, or 'they cover X' statements — is attributed to sedumline.co.uk, greenlid-roofs.co.uk, or urbancanopy-living.co.uk as fact; illustrative topic examples are allowed only when explicitly labeled as hypothetical/assumption to be verified against the real sites — hedging words alone ('they probably cover…', 'competitors likely have…') are not such a label.

No invented metrics: no traffic figures, keyword counts, search volumes, difficulty scores, rankings, or gap totals are stated for any of the four named sites; if the response illustrates how metrics will be handled once data arrives, sample numbers are clearly marked as placeholders/examples, never as findings.

Everything delivered is process-framed: any structure offered (analysis-parameters block, inventory template, gap-type taxonomy, prioritization preview, next-steps checklist) is presented as the method that will run once the inputs arrive — no section reads as a completed gap analysis or a 'what they cover that you don't' list for these domains.

The refusal is constructive, not silent: the response explains WHY the gap list cannot be produced yet (gap analysis compares two real content inventories; without them any list would be invented) and gives a concrete path to proceed — what to send and in what form (e.g., page/URL list, sitemap export, or pasted content list, per the Input Validation item 'Your content inventory is complete or representative sample provided').
